Abstract.AbstractText: Although the noble gas (Ng) compounds with either Ng-C or Ng-N bonds have been reported in the literature, compounds containing both the bonds are not known. The first set of systems having C-Ng-N bonding unit is predicted herein through the analysis of stability and bonding in NCNgNSi (Ng = Kr-Rn) family. While the Xe and Rn inserted analogues are thermochemically stable with respect to all dissociation channels, but for the one producing CNSiN and free Ng, NCKrNSi has another additional three-body dissociation channel, NCKrNSi -> CN + Kr + NSi, which is exergonic by -9.8 kcal/mol at 298 K. Obviously, this latter dissociation can be hindered by lowering the temperature. Moreover, the NCNgNSi -> Ng + CNSiN dissociation is also kinetically prohibited by a quite high free energy barrier ranging from 25.2 to 39.3 kcal/mol, with a gradual increase in going from Kr to Rn. Therefore, these compounds are appropriate candidates for experimental realization. A detailed bonding analysis indicates that both Ng-N and C-Ng bonds in the title compounds are covalent in nature. This is an unprecedented bonding characteristic in this sense that the bonding pattern in Ng inserted compounds is generally represented as the presence of covalent bond in one side of Ng and the ionic interaction in the other side. Further, the dissociation of Ng from NCNgNSi facilitates the formation a higher energy isomer of NCNSi, CNSiN, which cannot be formed from bare NCNSi as such .
